description.narrative: Kapacitetsutveckling av Serbiens Kemikaliemyndighet, genom samarbete med svenska KemI

Project support: Capacity building of Min o Environm to work with chemicals control issues according to EU REACH system. Capacity building of industry regarding classification, labelling and safety as well as cleaner production with respect to chemicals.

General question: Results related to the intended outcome 2015Question: Summarise results related to the intended outcome (this information will be sent to Open Aid)Answer: 1.The development and establishment of the products register in Serbia has been very successful: - Information on 30 000 chemical products to be registered and updated in the data base has been achieved. - Active involvement of administrative staff in development of IT system was crucial and has contributed to the overall result; - Continuous work of the Registry staff and constant personal communication with the industry as well as organizing workshops, trainings, developing guidelines and brochures and user friendly web page contributed to increasing the level of knowledge about chemicals among industry which lead to significant improvement of the quality of the data. 2. The development of guidance material and establishment of the helpdesk has been achieved. This fundamental for the information exchange with industry and the general public. The cooperation with the Chamber of Commerce is important and very much appreciated. 3. The training of the personnel has been a key factor: The core administration in Serbia has continued to learn from participation in international meetings and conferences related to chemicals and biocidal products management. It is important that the Serbian ministry establishes closer relation with EU-Member Statess in order to facilitate implementation of national legislation during the pre-accession period and ensure proper level of preparedness for tasks to be performed after the accession. The trainings of ministry administrators and inspectors and taking part as experts in the Commission and ECHA technical meetings must continue to become an up-to date expert when Serbia is entering the EU. 4. The screening exercise for Chapter 27 is finished and Serbia has already announced possibility to request transitional arrangements for implementation of certain articles of REACH and BPR.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
